Core safe-fetch helper / cache-only read (P072 c2, P077 c1/c3): the core has no safe-fetch helper, so both LIGHT modules use the module-side helper of batch p9-G03-1 (v3lum/modules/url_web/light_fetch.py: fetch_homepage / safe_get) to share one cache row per hop with the other LIGHT modules; please promote it to the core (then only the import changes). A PASSIVE module still cannot read the pages a LIGHT module already fetched (site_contacts_archive should reuse web_fingerprint's pages): request ctx.http.get(..., cache_only=True) (never a network send) or a read-only 'fetched pages of this case' view.

Read-only access to the run entity's case facts: tags (phishing/fraud/fake store, P072 c8 'hostile-tagged hosts', P077 c6) and attributes such as tls_inspect/CT cert_issuer (P072 c5 certIssuer matcher). Canonical reason_code for secure-web-gateway block pages (P072 c7), e.g. BLOCKED 'corporate_proxy'; 'challenge' is used now with the text 'blocked by corporate proxy (<vendor>)'.

Dataset post-processing hook for `v3lum data update` (P072 c5): run a module-supplied function once per new dataset version, in a subprocess with a hard wall-clock kill (regex time-budget screen of the webappanalyzer HTML patterns); now the screen runs in-process the first time a module loads a dataset version (~6 s), its refusals are kept as pattern-id hashes in ctx.state, and a per-page budget remembers slow patterns too.

core.http: a LIGHT seed binding allows only the seed host and its subdomains; a domain seed 'www.example.com' cannot crawl the bare registrable domain 'example.com' (P077 c3 says 'same registrable domain'). Either document it or allow the registrable domain of the seed for LIGHT reads.

run_on for 'own assets OR scope-file targets' (P076 c6): posture_third_party declares run_on='own_assets' as the condition names, so the policy gate skips in-scope targets that are not verified org-profile assets with the per-person breach reason 'breach check skipped: not an org domain'; request a run_on value or policy rule for 'own assets or scope-file targets' with a posture-specific skip reason.
notes: P072: web_fingerprint (LIGHT) + web_fingerprint_archive (PASSIVE, default) over one library in web_fingerprint.py: Wappalyzer-format matcher (headers/cookies/meta/html/scriptSrc/url/dns/certIssuer; js/dom/probe never evaluated), JS->Python regex converter, static ReDoS check + scaling time-budget screen (500 KB extrapolation) + per-page budget with slow patterns remembered in ctx.state; webappanalyzer GPL-3.0 data registered as 28 runtime datasets (github__p9-G03-2.json source, notice webappanalyzer.json, never bundled; tests and acceptance routes use a hand-written file); wafw00f header/cookie subset bundled as BSD-3 data (101 signatures, attack probes never ported, quadratic regexes simplified, proxy/CDN signatures tagged cdn_or_proxy); own MIT phishing-kit/panel rules; corporate SWG/challenge/proxy-error classification; version-inferred CVEs from the RetireJS repository (+ CISA KEV local copy) collapsed per technology (POSSIBLE, <= MEDIUM, KEV -> <= HIGH + tag kev); hostile pages and archived snapshots get technology_cves attributes instead of findings. Failures seen in the full suite that name other batches' modules (emailrep, git_metadata_identity, typosquat_live_checks, unshorten_*, notices dns_bruteforce/nuclei_runner) are other batches' work in progress. v3lum/data/providers/ssllabs.json (untracked) belongs to batch p2-G14-2 and is not part of this batch. REVIEW 2026-11-26 (adversarial): (1) both LIGHT modules now fetch through the shared safe-fetch helper (light_fetch.fetch_homepage/safe_get): before, web_fingerprint/site_contacts used ctx.http.get(allow_redirects=True) on the same cache key as the sibling LIGHT modules, which cache redirects hop by hop, so a cached 301 was read as the homepage (wrong fingerprint; site_contacts ended EMPTY without crawling); crawled pages that redirect off the seed or the registrable domain are no longer followed; redirect hops outside the seed are reported (SKIPPED scope, expand=False redirects_to pivot) and never requested; refused hops are recorded without query and without token/e-mail paths; https->http fallback never on timeouts/deadline/offline. (2) web_fingerprint_archive/site_contacts_archive: archived block, challenge, proxy or error pages are ERROR 'could not verify' (were EMPTY); a capture whose URL carries secrets is SKIPPED policy (was EMPTY). (3) the FC5 time-budget screen took ~30 s of CPU per process on the real data (the default archive module blew its 45 s deadline): escalating blob sizes with early exit (~6 s) and screen verdicts persisted per dataset version in ctx.state (later processes ~3.5 s). (4) ssllabs_assess sends startNew with retries=0 (a core 5xx/429 retry re-sent startNew=on). (5) site_contacts never writes e-mail- or token-bearing link paths to crawl_summary/raw; a request cap mid-crawl keeps the contacts read (partial request_cap); a rate limit mid-crawl ends partial rate_limited. (6) cached SSL Labs grades carry assessed_at (details.hostStartTime) and findings observed_last. (7) webappanalyzer source declares its dataset (policy no longer treats github as a receiver of the investigated value); both web_fingerprint modules declare cisa.kev (KEV copy they read).
